lead: The market's best day since April 2025 (Nasdaq +6.51%, S&P 500 +4.73%, out of correction) after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after he resigned; among non-chip big tech Oracle led, +12.3% to $113.68, yet still about 55% under its $250.25 52-week high.
why: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, president and director at 8:55 a.m. ET, lifting AI stocks including Oracle (Motley Fool); Nvidia closed +31.48% to $165.05, its best day since May 2003, a roughly $954B one-day gain (CNBC, Kiplinger via FinanceFeeds). Huang resigned Nov 12; SEC and House inquiries continue (House interview Dec 1).

Oracle said on Friday it had secured the financing for its OpenAI contract and that its Abilene campus is nearly complete (Motley Fool; single source), easing funding fears after it spent about $5B more on capital investment than operations brought in last quarter.

Market backdrop: Nasdaq 24,089.56 (+6.51%), S&P 500 7,237.17 (+4.73%), Dow 49,595.31 (+3.01%), VIX -25.8%; Tesla +11.5%, Meta +6.6%, Alphabet ~+6%, Amazon +3.5%, Apple +1.9%, Microsoft +1.6%; Anthropic -1.4%. Nomura's Charlie McElligott called it 'mechanical' buying (short covering, dealer hedges) that 'guarantees us nothing.' Next: October PCE Wed Nov 25 8:30 a.m. ET; markets closed Thursday, early close Friday.
